name: Risa Lombardo
bio: Risa Lombardo is the Green Party nominee for Arizona governor after winning the July 21, 2026 primary. News reports say she was a Republican precinct committeeman shortly before filing. The Arizona Green Party has publicly disavowed her candidacy.

platform.point: Says she supports fair and transparent elections.
Says she wants reform on education, homelessness and the prison system.

notes: Only vague statements found; no scored domains. State Green Party opposes her candidacy (gpelections.org, azgp.org).

name: Adam Withrow
bio: Adam Withrow is the Unity Party candidate for US Senate in Colorado. He is based in Walsenburg and says he has worked as a ranch hand, CNA, cook, contractor, detention officer and educator. He ran for Colorado's 3rd District in 2024.

platform.point: Wants a federal living wage tied to the consumer price index.
Calls for a unilateral declaration of peace and shutting down the US global military empire while keeping defenses.

economy.evidence: Proposes a federal living wage tied to the consumer price index, adjusting automatically with inflation.

foreign.evidence: Calls for a unilateral declaration of peace and shutting down the US global military empire.

notes: Q&A did not cover most domains. Other platform items (energy, healthcare) seen only in search summaries, not scored.

name: Neil J. Gillespie
bio: Neil J. Gillespie is a No Party Affiliation candidate in Florida's special US Senate election. He is an Ocala resident and founder of the advocacy group Justice Network. He describes himself as a working-class capitalist.

platform.point: Backs national health coverage with an opt-out option.
Supports secure borders, vetted legal immigrants and a path to citizenship for rule-followers.
Cites Washington's warning against foreign entanglements.
Says the US is not a Christian nation and supports separation of church and state.
Wants PACER fees abolished and support for pro se litigants.

welfare.evidence: Advocates national health coverage with an opt-out, modeled on other capitalist democracies.

immigration.evidence: Supports secure borders and lawful removal of illegal entrants, with legal pathways and citizenship for rule-followers.

foreign.evidence: Cites George Washington's farewell warnings against foreign entanglement.

faith.evidence: Says America is not a Christian nation and supports strict separation of church and state.

notes: Positions summarized from his campaign blog via page extraction; Florida voter guide found no clear stances on many issues.

name: Frank J. Russo
bio: Frank J. Russo is an independent candidate for Florida governor with a stated 40 years in business, over 30 in insurance. He named Rachel Rodriguez as his running mate. A June poll commissioned around his campaign put him at 7.1% in a three-way test.

platform.point: Proposes a 9.9% marginal state income tax on income above $1 million, dedicated to a reinvestment trust.
Unveiled a Medical Freedom Initiative stressing informed consent and parental opt-out rights.
Campaign accepts cryptocurrency donations.

economy.evidence: Calls himself a caring capitalist and proposes a 9.9% tax above $1 million to fund housing, trades and teacher pay.

liberty.evidence: Medical Freedom plan stresses individual and parental rights against one-size-fits-all government mandates.

notes: Evidence is campaign press releases.

name: Thomas Laehn
bio: Thomas Laehn is the Libertarian nominee for US Senate in Iowa and the Greene County Attorney, elected in 2018. He holds a political science PhD from LSU and taught constitutional law at McNeese State University. He describes himself as the first Libertarian elected to office in Iowa.

platform.point: Opposes executive orders creating criminal law and unilateral tariffs.
Calls prohibition a wasteful use of taxpayer resources.
Says to end federal tax credits for pipelines.

economy.evidence: Says government should stay out of pocketbooks and opposes unilateral tariffs.

liberty.evidence: Says government should stay out of bedrooms; calls marijuana prohibition wasteful and leaves abortion to states.

notes: Iowa Capital Dispatch page returned 403; used its headline only. Some details came via page extraction of Iowa Public Radio.

name: Lydia Christensen
bio: Lydia Christensen is the Libertarian nominee for US Senate in Michigan, nominated June 28, 2026. She is a computer scientist and founder of Iron Fortress LLC, a Bitcoin mining and compute company. She says she grew up in foster care and runs on a small volunteer budget.

platform.point: Runs as 'Unchain Michigan' and says she answers to no donor.

notes: Website policy pages could not be read; no scored domains.

name: Rebecca Whiting
bio: Rebecca Whiting is the Libertarian nominee for US Senate in Minnesota and chairs the state Libertarian Party. She is an Army combat veteran and Iraq War medic who lives on a homestead farm in Bemidji. She polled about 2% in a September 2026 poll.

platform.point: Wants to end forever wars and pass a Defend the Guard bill.
Opposes taxpayer funding of data centers, flock cameras and surveillance infrastructure.
Wants citizenship and work authorization made free and fast.
Focuses on national debt, inflation and the dollar.

economy.evidence: Focuses on balancing the budget and reducing regulatory burdens and taxes on small producers.

security.evidence: Opposes taxpayer funding of data centers, flock cameras and other surveillance infrastructure.

immigration.evidence: Supports reforming the process to obtain citizenship or work authorization, making it free and fast.

foreign.evidence: Prioritizes ending forever wars and limiting Guard deployment to congressionally declared wars.

notes: Positions from MPR/KAXE election guide summarizing her statements.

name: Danielle Ford
current_role: Member, Nevada State Board of Education
bio: Danielle Ford is a nonpartisan candidate for Nevada governor. She is a member of the Nevada State Board of Education and a former Clark County School District trustee (2018-2022). Her campaign reported no fundraising as of recent coverage.

platform.point: Wants stricter scrutiny of education contracts, saying ending some could free up $2 billion a year (unverified estimate).
Wants to replace standardized testing with direct teacher-parent communication.
Wants a statewide AI plan before adoption and opposes more Las Vegas data centers.

tech.evidence: Advocates a statewide AI plan before adoption and opposes additional data centers in Las Vegas.

education.evidence: Focuses on public education contracting reform and funding for teachers and aides; would end standardized testing.

notes: Single news source for positions.

name: Michael Louis Dublin Jr.
bio: Michael Dublin is the Green Party candidate for US Senate in North Carolina, on the ballot with Roy Cooper, Michael Whatley and Libertarian Shannon Bray. He polled about 1 to 1.5% in September 2026 polls.
notes: Little public information found on his own statements; no scored domains.

name: Robert E. Brooks Sr.
bio: Robert E. Brooks Sr. is an independent candidate for Oklahoma governor running as the Farmer Servant movement. He grew up in Lindsay and says he has worked as a welder, machinist, police officer, sheriff's deputy, detective, firefighter, EMT and insurance professional. He has not held elected office.

platform.point: Plans a People's App to ask residents before major decisions.
Supports a government plan anyone can buy into.
Supports universal school choice for every family.
Supports data centers and strengthening the oil and gas industry while protecting water.

welfare.evidence: Supports a government health plan anyone can buy into.

energy.evidence: Supports strengthening Oklahoma's oil and gas industry and data centers.

education.evidence: Supports universal school choice for every family.

notes: School choice and public option come from a search snippet of votetheperson.org, not fetched directly.

name: Mark Hackett
bio: Mark Hackett is the Constitution Party nominee for US Senate in South Carolina. He is from Greenville and previously ran for US House in SC-4 (2024) and SC-6 (2020).
notes: No campaign statements or website found; no scored domains.

name: Wendell Jackson
current_role: Spoken word performer and comedian (per Politics1)
bio: Wendell Jackson of Clarksville is an independent candidate for Tennessee governor, qualified by petition. He describes his effort as a nonpartisan, constitution-upholding, no-money campaign.

platform.point: Wants enhanced employment services, housing stability and healthcare for all.

welfare.evidence: Says he wants housing stability and healthcare for all Tennesseans.

notes: Only slogan-level statements found. Raised $0 per Tennessee Firefly.

name: Karl Knox Smithson
bio: Karl Knox Smithson of McMinnville is an independent candidate for Tennessee governor, qualified by petition on February 19, 2026.
notes: No campaign website, platform or statement found (Tennessee Firefly says the same).

name: Mary L. Sanders
bio: Mary L. Sanders is the Green Party candidate for Connecticut's 1st District. She has worked as a consultant and as executive director of the Spanish Speaking Center of New Britain. She also ran in 2022 (1.2%) and 2024.
notes: Little public information on her own statements found; no scored domains.

name: Priscilla Gonzalez
bio: Priscilla Gonzalez is listed as a Democratic candidate for Louisiana's 3rd District, challenging Republican Rep. Clay Higgins. Her campaign site describes her as the daughter of immigrants with a veterans' advocacy and immigrant rights background.
notes: Sources conflict: Louisiana Illuminator reported the state Democratic Party endorsed John Day over her, and Ballotpedia lists a May 16 primary. Ballot status should be re-verified. No stated positions retrieved.

name: Nancy Wallace
bio: Nancy Wallace is the Green Party nominee in Maryland's 8th District against Democratic Rep. Jamie Raskin and Republican Cheryl Riley. She has a political science degree from Yale, environmental advocacy experience including Sierra Club director roles, and ran in 2016 and 2024 (2.5%).
notes: Positions not retrieved; no scored domains.

name: Sharon Renier
bio: Sharon Renier is the U.S. Taxpayers Party candidate for Michigan's 5th District, nominated July 18, 2026. She has previously run for office in Michigan as a Democrat (2004, US House) and in a 2010 Republican state Senate primary.
notes: No current statements found; no scored domains.

name: Mia Pettus
bio: Carissima Mia Pettus is the Libertarian nominee for Michigan's 8th District. She is a former Philadelphia police officer and Navy civilian federal police officer, and publishes the PALS Report on Substack.

platform.point: Says she will focus on local economic growth, affordability, federal oversight and opposing a surveillance state.

security.evidence: Says she will push back against the threat of a surveillance state.

notes: Source page returned 403; relied on search snippet.

name: Cubby Nkromo
bio: Kwabena 'Cubby' Nkromo is the Green Party nominee in Michigan's 10th District. He studied plant and soil sciences at Tuskegee University and agricultural economics at Clemson, and founded Atlanta Food & Farm. He now lives in Flint.

platform.point: Supports commercial composting through public policy to divert waste from landfills.

notes: Few published positions; no scored domains.

name: Brenda Sanders
bio: Brenda Sanders is the Green Party nominee for Michigan's 12th District, facing Rep. Rashida Tlaib. She is a former 36th District Court judge in Detroit who was ordered off the bench in 2015.
notes: No current policy statements found; no scored domains.

name: Bobby (Afzal) Khan
bio: Bobby Khan is an independent candidate for Nevada's 1st District against Rep. Dina Titus. He is a former exotic car dealer whose campaign is branded 'Wanted for Congress'.

platform.point: Wants zero taxes on veteran income and on gambling winnings.
Wants to end civil asset forfeiture without conviction.
Wants affordable housing.

economy.evidence: Platform centers on tax cuts (veterans, gambling winnings) and easing small business burdens.

liberty.evidence: Wants to end civil asset forfeiture without conviction.

notes: Platform items taken from search summary of a press-style page.

name: Sandeep Dixit
bio: Sandeep Dixit is an independent candidate for Ohio's 13th District. He describes himself as an engineer and technology executive, and joined the Independent Candidate Network of independent House candidates.

platform.point: Supports guaranteed basic healthcare access.
Calls for rigorous enforcement of environmental regulations.
Supports implementing privacy protection law.
Wants training for emerging work and automation to benefit the district.

welfare.evidence: Supports guaranteed basic healthcare access and retirement security.

energy.evidence: Calls for rigorous enforcement of environmental regulations.

notes: Positions are brief campaign-site bullets.
